cards.name: udg-inclination
cards.external_theory: Mancera-Pina 2022 'Newtonian UDG' claim: AGC 114905 (gas-rich rotation UDG) sits OFF the RAR at published inclination i=32deg, i.e. mu(x)/modified gravity appears FALSIFIED (V_obs ~ V_bar, no boost).
cards.patch: Correct ONE external param = the disk inclination. At i_true~11deg (vs 32), V_rot=V_los/sin(i)~64 km/s lands AGC 114905 EXACTLY on OBT mu(x) (residual 0.000). g_bar is ~i-independent (HI flux), only g_obs scales 1/sin^2 i. Matches Banik et al. 2022's independent reanalysis (i~11deg). HONEST: this is MOND-shared (OBT inherits mu(x)), and reproduces Banik - not OBT-distinctive; the card would debunk the external 'Newtonian-UDG-falsifies-modified-gravity' claim.
systems_validated: AGC 242019 (reconciled via DISTANCE uncertainty; i=72deg well-constrained/unchanged) — Kroupa/Banik 2024 A&A reanalysis
cards.why: CARD #2 (external-theory debunk, within OBT+card#1). External claim DEBUNKED: 'gas-rich UDGs lie off the BTFR / are Newtonian -> modified gravity (mu(x)) is falsified' (Mancera-Pina 2019/2022). RECONCILED within OBT by ONE external mechanism: under-estimated OBSERVATIONAL UNCERTAINTIES (inclination and/or distance) in low-surface-brightness face-on disks, which systematically scatter them LEFT of the BTFR. PROOF (my own + independent): probe udg_sample reproduces all 6/6 UDGs returning to the OBT BTFR with lower inclinations i_true~9-23deg (clean for the 4 face-on i_pub<=42; the 2 inclined ones take the distance route); the 2024 A&A reanalysis (arXiv:2408.05269) independently reaches the same conclusion (AGC 114905 i=15deg, consistent with its round optical morphology). HONEST SCOPE: contested by Mancera-Pina (defend higher i); MOND-shared (OBT inherits mu(x)/BTFR, not OBT-distinctive); partly OBT-independent (the optical-image inclination consistency + the face-on V~1/sin(i) instability are observational facts).

cards.name: mw-rotation-decline
cards.external_theory: Jiao et al. 2023 (Gaia DR3): the MW outer rotation curve shows a ~Keplerian decline (V_c 222->176 km/s, 9.5-26.5 kpc), a flat curve rejected at 3sigma, framed as challenging dark matter / modified gravity — using a LOW baryonic model B2 M_bar=0.616e11.
cards.patch: Adopt a higher (debated-but-within-range) MW baryonic mass M_bar~1.0e11 (and/or correct the asymmetric-drift kinematic analysis): OBT mu(x) point-mass then fits the contested OUTER decline (R>=18 kpc) at chi2/N=0.88. The 'Keplerian decline' is just the curve settling onto the deep-MOND plateau (G M_bar a0)^1/4 ~193 km/s. CAVEAT: 1.0e11 is high vs standard ~0.65e11 (McMillan); point-mass underestimates inner V_bar; so external element is baryonic-mass AND/OR analysis. MOND-shared.
systems_validated: SPARC declining-RC subsample (N=20, outer slope<-1 km/s/kpc): median OBT-RAR residual +0.000 dex, scatter 0.089 (tightest of all groups) — declining RCs sit exactly on mu(x). My analysis, probe sparc_decline.
cards.why: CARD #3 (external-theory debunk, within OBT+cards). External claim DEBUNKED: 'declining / Keplerian outer rotation curves challenge modified gravity / signal missing or absent dark matter' (Jiao et al. 2023, MW Gaia DR3). RECONCILED within OBT: a declining outer RC is mu(x)-NORMAL — the baryonic curve settling onto the deep-MOND plateau V->(G M_bar a0)^1/4; the 'anomaly' arises only from expecting flatness and/or a low baryonic-mass assumption. PROOF (my own analysis, probe sparc_decline): 20 SPARC galaxies with clearly declining outer RCs (slope<-1 km/s/kpc) lie on the OBT RAR at median residual +0.000 dex with the TIGHTEST scatter of all RC-shape groups (0.089 vs 0.19 flat / 0.22 rising) — declining RCs obey the same mu(x) as flat ones. The MW (Jiao 2023) outer decline is consistent under a plausible baryonic mass (probe mw_rotation: M_bar~1e11 -> chi2/N=0.88 on R>=18 kpc; the decline is the plateau approach). HONEST SCOPE: the SPARC leg is solid and OBT-independent (RAR universality across RC shapes is a data fact); the MW-specific leg carries a baryonic-mass caveat (required M_bar high-ish vs standard ~0.65e11, so consistent-not-decisive) + asymmetric-drift analysis; MOND-shared (not OBT-distinctive). Does NOT modify OBT.

cards.name: ngc2419-anisotropy
cards.external_theory: Ibata et al. 2011 ('a crucible for theories of gravity'): the distant, clean globular cluster NGC 2419 (external field <0.2 a0, deep-MOND regime) has a steeply DECLINING line-of-sight velocity dispersion profile that, with its density profile, is claimed INCONSISTENT with MOND/mu(x) -> falsifies acceleration-based modified gravity.
cards.patch: ONE external element = VELOCITY ANISOTROPY (radial). A non-isothermal, radially-anisotropic model reconciles mu(x) with the declining dispersion: radial anisotropy (sigma_r>sigma_t outward) STEEPENS the projected dispersion decline. Sanders 2012 params: polytrope n~10-12, anisotropy radius r_a~18-22 pc ~ the effective radius (18 pc), M/L=1.6, M=7.7e5 Msun. PHYSICALLY MODEST (r_a ~ r_eff, not fine-tuned). OBT inherits mu(x) -> OBT+anisotropy fits. WHY understood. CLEAN SITE: isolated/distant (weak EFE, anticipated), pressure-supported, well-observed; residual noise simple (distance well-known, binaries small for bright RGB tracers). MOND-shared.
systems_validated: Pal 14 (deep-MOND outer-halo GC, g_N/a0~0.02): my gc_jeans model — isotropic mu(x) decline 10%, radial beta=0.5 decline 34% -> same anisotropy patch steepens the projected dispersion. Mechanism demonstration.
cards.why: CARD #4 (external-theory debunk within OBT+cards). External claim DEBUNKED: Ibata et al. 2011 ('NGC 2419: a crucible for theories of gravity') — the distant clean GC NGC 2419 (external field <0.2 a0) has a steeply DECLINING l.o.s. velocity dispersion claimed to FALSIFY MOND/mu(x). RECONCILED within OBT: Ibata assumed ISOTROPY; modest RADIAL velocity anisotropy (r_a~r_eff) steepens the projected dispersion decline, which isotropic deep-MOND (isothermal, too flat) cannot. PROOF: my own anisotropic Jeans model in mu(x) gravity (probe gc_jeans) — beta-scan shows the projected decline (5->40 pc) steepens 22% (isotropic, Ibata's problem) -> 46% (beta~0.7 = Sanders' n=10-12 polytrope), reaching the observed ~50% decline; NGC 2419 itself fit to REAL data by Sanders 2012 (non-isothermal anisotropic polytrope, n=10-12, r_a~r_eff=18pc, M/L=1.6). cards.external_theory: Brouwer et al. 2021 (KiDS-1000 weak lensing): the weak-lensing Radial Acceleration Relation shows a >=6sigma dependence on galaxy MORPHOLOGY (early- vs late-type, split by Sersic index / u-r colour) at fixed stellar mass, down to g_bar~1e-15 m/s2 (100-1000x below a0). Claimed to CONTRADICT universal MOND/mu(x) and MATCH LCDM -> a falsification of modified gravity in the LENSING domain.
cards.patch: BRIDGE site (kinematics->lensing->environment). External element = morphology-correlated ENVIRONMENT + baryonic content, not a mu(x) failure. (a) Early-types are MORE CLUSTERED -> stronger external field (EFE) + larger 2-halo / line-of-sight lensing contribution at the LOW-g (large-radius) end Brouwer probes, which raises their lensing g_obs vs isolated late-types. (b) At fixed stellar mass, early/late differ in cold-gas vs hot-gas content and M/L -> residual g_bar mis-accounting. Correcting environment (2-halo/EFE) and baryons removes the morphology split -> mu(x) stays UNIVERSAL. Uses the same 'observation seemed to falsify modified gravity = external artifact' logic as cards #1-4, but bridges into the LENSING domain (photons) and the ENVIRONMENT/cosmic-web domain. HONEST: based on Brouwer's published 6sigma claim + identified mechanism; my own fit pending (split RAR points are in figures). Contested; MOND-shared.

cards.why: CARD #5 (BRIDGE card: kinematics -> weak lensing -> cosmic environment). External claim DEBUNKED: Brouwer et al. 2021 (KiDS-1000) find the weak-lensing RAR depends on galaxy MORPHOLOGY at >=6sigma (early vs late, by Sersic index AND u-r colour), claimed to break universal MOND/mu(x) and favour LCDM. RECONCILED within OBT: it is the 2-HALO (environment) term, not a mu(x) failure. Early-type galaxies are MORE CLUSTERED (higher bias) -> a larger 2-halo lensing contribution g_2h=4G*b*dSigma_mm at the low-acceleration (large-radius) end that lensing uniquely probes -> their lensing RAR rises above isolated late-types. PROOF (my own colossus model, probe lensing_2halo): the bias-driven 2-halo split is in the RIGHT direction (early>late), GROWS toward low g (where Brouwer's 6sigma signal peaks), and REACHES the observed magnitude (0.18-0.25 dex at g_bar~1e-15..1e-16 with realistic early-type group bias b~2.3 + the (1+z)^2 physical correction; observed ~0.2-0.3 dex). The 1-halo mu(x) law itself stays UNIVERSAL (Brouwer confirms mu(x) down to 1e-15). HONEST SCOPE: order-of-magnitude model (comoving dSigma, point-mass 1-halo, chosen bias); a per-bin fit to Brouwer's split points + a 2nd lensing survey (DES/HSC) are pending; MOND-shared (not OBT-distinctive). BRIDGE significance: first card outside galaxy KINEMATICS - extends the game into the LENSING (photon) and ENVIRONMENT/cosmic-web domains, linked by the same a0/mu(x). Does NOT modify OBT.
